in_latin.name: Justa
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Justa derivatur a vocabulo iustus, quod significat rectus, rectissimus, verus et verissimus. In traditione Christiana, nomen Justa indicat personam iustam, rectam et veram. In historia Ecclesiae, nomen Justa invenitur in scriptis patrum, qui describunt virtutes et exempla iustitiae. In cultura populari, nomen Justa est nomen femininum, quod designat mulierem iustam et rectam.

in_english.name: Justa
in_english.long_meaning: The name Justa is derived from the Latin word iustus, meaning just, fair, righteous, upright, and virtuous. In Christian tradition, the name Justa signifies a just, fair, and righteous person. In church history, the name Justa is found in the writings of the Fathers, who describe the virtues and examples of justice. In popular culture, the name Justa is a feminine name that designates a just and upright woman, reflecting the values of fairness, righteousness, and virtue.

data.cultural_impact: The name Justa was common among Christians in the Roman Empire. It conveys a sense of fairness, morality, and justice, which were important virtues in ancient Roman society as well as in early Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Justa honors two remarkable saints. St. Justa of Rome was a martyr who, as tradition holds, was beheaded for refusing to sacrifice to idols. Her unwavering commitment to her faith and her steadfast refusal to compromise her beliefs despite persecution are inspiring examples of righteousness and devotion. St. Justa of Beauvais was a French nun known for her obedience, humility, and penitence. Her life illustrates the importance of living a just and righteous life, as guided by the tenets of Christianity. Both these women, with their unique stories, offer a powerful spiritual significance to the name Justa.
